facts.t: A Rajya Sabha seat was once decided by drawing lots
facts.d: The 2024 Himachal Pradesh election produced a 34–34 tie after cross-voting. Under the rules the winner was chosen by draw — an Upper House seat settled by chance rather than by votes.

facts.t: Cross-voting in a Rajya Sabha election is not defection
facts.d: The Tenth Schedule bites on proceedings of the Assembly, and a Rajya Sabha election is not one. An MLA who defies the party there faces internal discipline but no automatic disqualification — the single largest gap in the anti-defection regime.

facts.t: The Lords lost their court in 2009
facts.d: Until the Constitutional Reform Act took effect, Britain's highest appellate body sat inside the upper chamber. The Rajya Sabha never had a judicial role — but it does hold powers the Lords never had, including Article 249 and Article 312.

bank.q: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
bank.e: The constitutional maximum is 250 — up to 238 representatives of states and Union Territories plus 12 presidential nominees. The present sanctioned strength is 245, of whom 233 are elected.

bank.q: With reference to the Rajya Sabha, consider the following statements:
s: It never dissolves, and one-third of its members retire every two years.
Bills pending in the Rajya Sabha do not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to both Houses.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under Article 75(3) the Council is responsible to the Lok Sabha alone.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a special power of the Rajya Sabha?
o: Authorising Parliament to legislate on a State List subject under Article 249
Creating new All India Services under Article 312
Initiating a no-confidence motion against the government
Participating in the removal of the Vice-President
bank.e: No-confidence motions lie only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha holds the other three, and Articles 249 and 312 are exclusive to it.

bank.q: Match List I (chamber) with List II (its power over money bills):
pairs: 2. Recommendations only, with a fourteen-day return
4. May delay by one month only
bank.e: The Rajya Sabha may only recommend within fourteen days, the Lords may delay a month, and the Senate has equal taxation powers — plus sole jurisdiction over impeachment trials.

bank.q: Kuldip Nayar (2006) upheld which two changes to Rajya Sabha elections?
o: The open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement
Direct election and equal state representation
Proportional representation and the domicile requirement
bank.e: It upheld both the open ballot and the deletion of the domicile requirement. Shailesh Manubhai Parmar (2018) later struck down NOTA in Rajya Sabha elections.

bank.as: The open ballot in Rajya Sabha elections does not guarantee transparency to the public.
bank.rs: Disclosure is made to the party agent, which enables surveillance of legislators rather than public accountability.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal for a restricted open ballot with ECI observers and no photography.

bank.q: Consider the following criticisms of the Rajya Sabha:
s: State representation is proportional to population, so large states dominate.
The Money Bill route can be used to bypass the House.
Members must be at least thirty-five years of age.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The minimum age is thirty, not thirty-five.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed improvements to Rajya Sabha elections EXCEPT:
o: Preserving proportional representation by single transferable vote
Replacing STV with first past the post for clarity
A State Representation Statement instead of a rigid domicile bar
Transparent presidential nominations through a non-partisan search committee
bank.e: First past the post would let a state's ruling party monopolise every seat — preserving PR-STV is expressly recommended.

bank.q: Which chamber is described as a co-equal legislature with its counterpart?
bank.e: The Senate holds equal legislative power with the House of Representatives, plus exclusive powers over impeachment trials, confirmations and treaty ratification.

bank.q: With reference to the deliberative role, consider the following statements:
s: Twelve members are nominated for distinction in literature, science, art and social service.
Its composition changes more slowly than the Lok Sabha's.
It has eight of the twenty-four departmentally related standing committees.
bank.e: All three are correct — the slower turnover and nominated expertise are what make the chamber a place of second thought.

bank.q: Direct election to the United States Senate was introduced by:
bank.e: The Seventeenth Amendment of 1913. Before that senators were chosen by state legislatures — the method India still uses for the Rajya Sabha.
